text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert PDR-7892 -> gpu-pool-usw2-prod saturated, queue growth > 95th pct, autoscaler failing to add nodes

ops-bot: Autoscaler error: \"scaleup rejected: quota_limit_reached\" for pool prod-gpu-usw2

Mia Chen: oncall here — paging eng-sre and runtime. marking P0 and starting triage. @Liam O'Neill @Asha Patel please ack

Liam O'Neill: acked. pulling autoscaler logs now. first glance: many requests tied to model:v21.4 with context sizes spiking, kv-cache miss rate up ~4x

Asha Patel: runtime here. v21.4 was rolled ~45m ago to improve summarization. looks like default prefix warmup is causing large KV growth during prefill. also seeing throughput regression ~18% per-GPU

RJ Park: customer-impact check — CS reporting elevated 5xxs for three enterprise tenants in us-west. Carla can you confirm severity?

Carla Gomez: confirmed. Tenants: Acme, BrightHealth, and NovaLabs seeing 502s and timeouts. Support ticket threads open, customers are seeing failed completions and elevated latency > 10s

Mia Chen: immediate goals: 1) stop further queue growth 2) reduce per-request GPU pressure 3) restore customer traffic. proposing temporary traffic shift to fallback model and pause v21.4 rollout

Liam O'Neill: agreed. two quick knobs: 1) revert routing for production alias to model:v20.11 (lighter context handling) 2) disable prefill-warmup for v21.4 instances so KV doesn't grow on new sessions

Asha Patel: I can flip warmup flag on the runtime: 
```bash
# disable kv warmup for v21.4 rollout group
redwood runtime update --model v21.4 --set prefill_kv=false --env production
```
I'll push in 30s after approval

Mia Chen: go ahead Asha. Liam, can you attempt a temporary routing pin to v20.11 and open a canary to ensure no regressions?

Liam O'Neill: running routing command now:
```bash
redwood routing set --alias prod-textgen --target model:v20.11 --weight 100
```
Applying...

ops-bot: routing change applied by Liam O'Neill at 3187654380

Liam O'Neill: autoscaler logs: scale attempts still failing due to quota. I opened a request to infra to bump GPU quota for the pool but that will take time (30-45m). We need to reduce load now

Mia Chen: Carla, communicate to CS: we are routing traffic to a stable variant and expect consumer success rate to improve within 2-3 minutes. ask customers to retry. mark incident in the support tickets

Carla Gomez: sending update now. message: \"We're routing your requests to a stable variant to reduce errors; should improve shortly. We'll follow up with PS for any stateful issues.\"

Asha Patel: disabling prefill_kv on v21.4 rollout group... done. Confirmed on 4/4 instances. KV usage stopped ramping for new sessions. Existing KV growth still present until KV TTL expires

Liam O'Neill: queue length metrics: before mitigation qlen=18k, after routing switch and warmup toggle qlen=6.1k and trending down. Token throughput per GPU down ~12% which is helping latency

Mia Chen: good. keep an eye on tail latencies. we should also throttle large-context requests at the ingress for the next 2 hours to prevent re-amplification

Asha Patel: deploying a short rule to cap context_len to 8k tokens for prod alias (requests > cap will be rejected with 413 and guidance to client):
```json
{"route":"prod-textgen","max_context_tokens":8000}
```
Deployment complete

RJ Park: note for customers that some long conversations may get rejected; we're coordinating with PS to help rehydrate state where needed

Carla Gomez: update sent to affected customers. one asked for ETA on rollback — telling them we'll keep them posted and offer to replay outstanding inputs if needed

Liam O'Neill: autoscaler still hitting soft_quota; infra bumped some spare capacity via manual pool add (hotpool +2 GPUs) — ops confirmed at 3187654500. Should ease pressure for background scaling attempts

ops-bot: Manual pool modification: +2 GPUs added to prod-gpu-usw2 by infra-team at 3187654500

Mia Chen: we're seeing error rates for those tenants drop from 18% -> 2% over 12 minutes. queue now 1.2k and dropping. starting post-incident checklist: capture traces, dump a few hot requests, preserve config state

Asha Patel: collected a heap of KV entries and sample traces. saving to /incidents/PDR-7892/artifacts. Also saved runtime config diff: v21.4 introduced prefill_kv=true by default and a new tokenizer prefill path that increases prefix length by ~300 tokens for system prompts

Liam O'Neill: adding temporary autoscaler override to allow scale to 250 instances until quota request completes:
```bash
redwood autoscaler update --pool prod-gpu-usw2 --soft_limit 250 --override temporary --reason \"incident PDR-7892\"
```
Override in place

Mia Chen: who will own the handoff to postmortem? I can start the ticket, but want runtime/eng-sre to lead root cause analysis

Asha Patel: runtime will own the RCA for KV warmup behaviour and tokenization change. I'll start notes and attach warmup config diffs.

Liam O'Neill: eng-sre will own autoscaler and quota analysis. I’ll collect scaling logs and threshold transitions

RJ Park: product will coordinate customer comms and prioritization of a safe rollback path if needed. We should schedule a hotfix deploy that reverts the prefill change for v21.4 and re-run rollout in canary only

Carla Gomez: customers acknowledged. two asked for a timeline for a fix — gave provisional ETA 3-6 hours for a safe rollback/canary plan

Mia Chen: thanks all. current status: mitigations applied, customer errors decreasing, autoscaler override & manual GPUs in place. next: create incident ticket PDR-7892, set follow-up meeting at +2h, and handoff to daytime oncall at 3187654622

incident-bot: Incident PDR-7892 created: https://incidents.internal/PDR-7892 by Mia Chen

Mia Chen: handing off to daytime oncall @Liam O'Neill — leave a short runbook in the ticket about the routing flip, warmup toggle, and autoscaler override. I'm available if it re-escalates :thumbsup:

Liam O'Neill: taking handoff. notes captured. setting a 2h follow-up. thanks team.
